hero.headline: Berkshire Hathaway Acquires Homebuilder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 Billion
hero.body:
Berkshire Hathaway has acquired Taylor Morrison, a national homebuilder, in a transaction valued between $6.8 billion and $8.5 billion. The deal represents the first major takeover completed under the leadership of Greg Abel, who recently became CEO of the conglomerate.

Warren Buffett announced his retirement plans at Berkshire's annual shareholder meeting, stating he would step down as CEO and chair at the end of 2025. The 94-year-old billionaire, who has led the company since 1965, recommended that Abel succeed him in the top role. "I think the time has arrived where Greg should become the chief executive officer of the company at year end," Buffett said at the event in Omaha, Nebraska. He emphasized his confidence in Abel's capabilities, saying "The decision to keep every share is an economic decision because I think the prospects of Berkshire will be better under Greg's management than mine."

Abel, 62, has been designated as Buffett's successor since 2001 and brings 25 years of experience at Berkshire. As vice-chair, he currently oversees the company's non-insurance businesses, including fossil energy, chemical, real estate, and retail operations. The Taylor Morrison acquisition marks his first major deal as the company's new chief executive.

The valuation discrepancy between the $6.8 billion and $8.5 billion figures likely reflects different methodologies for calculating enterprise value versus equity value, or variations in how assumed debt is counted. The acquisition adds residential construction and land development operations to Berkshire's existing housing sector exposure through its building materials and home furnishings subsidiaries.

Taylor Morrison operates as a national homebuilder across multiple markets. The purchase strengthens Berkshire's position in the housing industry, an area where the company maintains long-term interest through various subsidiaries, including paint manufacturer Benjamin Moore and other building materials firms.

The timing of the acquisition comes as Buffett continues to lead the conglomerate during its leadership transition. In February, Berkshire reported record annual operating profit of $47.44 billion for 2024, representing a 27 percent increase. The company now operates 189 businesses spanning insurance, railroads, energy, manufacturing, and other sectors.

At the shareholder meeting, Buffett also addressed broader economic concerns, warning about potential consequences of trade policies and the importance of international commerce. He emphasized that maintaining positive global relationships benefits all parties involved in trade.

The Taylor Morrison deal reflects Berkshire's historical investment strategy of acquiring companies in sectors where it identifies long-term value and stable cash flows. The housing market has faced challenges from elevated mortgage rates in recent years, though homebuilders have adapted by offering rate buydowns and developing more affordable housing options.

cards.headline: Trump seeks changes to US-Iran nuclear deal
cards.teaser: The requested modifications involve the Strait of Hormuz and highly enriched uranium removal, according to US media reports.
cards.body:
President Trump is requesting modifications to a proposed nuclear agreement with Iran under negotiation. The requested changes focus on provisions concerning the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global shipping route, and the removal of highly enriched uranium from Iran.

The negotiations represent ongoing diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran to address Iran's nuclear program. According to US media reports, Trump has been actively engaged in seeking these edits to the deal terms.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russian oil infrastructure in overnight attacks
cards.teaser: Drone strikes hit a pipeline, refinery, and fuel depot inside Russia as Ukraine continues targeting energy facilities.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces conducted overnight drone attacks targeting Russian energy infrastructure, hitting a pipeline, oil refinery, and fuel depot. The strikes are part of Kyiv's ongoing campaign to disrupt Russia's fuel production and supply capabilities supporting its war effort.

The attacks also destroyed a Tu-142MR aircraft used by Russia's Northern Fleet for maritime patrol and anti-submarine operations. Ukraine has signaled plans to continue targeting similar Russian energy facilities.

cards.headline: Israel seizes historic castle in Lebanon as ground offensive expands
cards.body:
Israeli troops have captured Beaufort Castle, a clifftop fortress in southern Lebanon, marking the country's deepest military incursion into Lebanese territory in more than 26 years. The Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced the capture of the strategic stronghold, also known as Qalaat al-Shaqif, which Israel previously used as a military base during its occupation from 1982 to 2000.

The castle sits on elevated terrain overlooking much of southern Lebanon, giving it significant strategic importance. Israeli and Golani Brigade flags now fly over the fortress as the military continues operations in the surrounding region. The IDF stated it launched the operation to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and expand territorial control, with forces now pushing towards the Zahrani River, approximately six miles north of the Litani River where they previously held positions.

The advance has drawn sharp criticism from European governments. France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot requested an emergency UN Security Council meeting to address Israel's military operations in Lebanon. He stated: "Nothing can justify the prolongation of Israeli military operations in Lebanon and its increasingly deep occupation of Lebanese territory."

Israeli forces appear to be positioning themselves to potentially encircle Nabatieh, a southern Lebanese city that holds significant economic and cultural importance for the region. For many in Lebanon, Nabatieh carries symbolic weight extending beyond its military value, having repeatedly been caught in the crossfire of Israeli campaigns throughout history.

Mohanad Hage Ali, a senior fellow at the Carnegie Middle East Center, warned of concerning possibilities. He suggested the level of destruction raises questions about whether Israel intends to deny the population's return or pursue settlement similar to actions in the West Bank. "Annexation is no longer a wild conspiracy theory," he said, referencing ministerial statements from Israeli officials.

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of pursuing "a scorched-earth policy and collective punishment" through the destruction of towns and villages and forced displacement of inhabitants. He called for an immediate ceasefire and defended his government's engagement in US-brokered negotiations with Israel, describing them as "the least costly path for our country and our people."

The offensive has displaced more than 1.2 million people since March 2 through Israeli strikes and evacuation orders. A ceasefire nominally began on April 17 but has never been observed, with Israel and Hezbollah accusing each other of daily violations.

The escalation complicates ongoing US-Iran negotiations, as Tehran has indicated any deal must include an end to fighting in Lebanon. Observers suggest Israeli officials and military commanders want to inflict maximum damage on Hezbollah before potential diplomatic agreements impose new restrictions on their operations.

cards.headline: 2025 wildfires set record as costliest ever
cards.teaser: Severe blazes in densely populated areas like Los Angeles drove record losses last year, researchers found.
cards.body:
Wildfires in 2025 caused more financial damage than any previous year on record, according to researchers. The record losses were driven primarily by severe, hard-to-control fires in densely populated regions, including the Los Angeles area. These urban-adjacent blazes proved particularly destructive due to the concentration of homes and infrastructure in their paths.

The findings highlight the growing financial toll of wildfires as development continues in fire-prone areas. When fires reach populated zones, the damage extends beyond natural landscapes to include residential neighborhoods, commercial properties, and critical infrastructure. The 2025 fire season set a new benchmark for wildfire costs, surpassing previous records.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Set for June 12 Prompts Wall Street Reorganization
cards.teaser: Wall Street firms are reorganizing operations around the upcoming SpaceX initial public offering scheduled for June 12.
cards.body:
SpaceX's upcoming IPO is significant enough that major financial institutions are reorganizing operations to handle the deal and expected trading activity. The company has already established itself as a major government contractor, earning $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts ahead of the public offering. According to its IPO filing, government contracts represented one-fifth of SpaceX's projected 2025 revenue.

Financial analysts have flagged governance risks for potential IPO investors, while some warn that premium pricing may disadvantage retail buyers. The scale of the offering has positioned SpaceX as a major market event for Wall Street.

cards.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving office
cards.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell has issued a stark warning that the central bank faces a credibility crisis in his first public comments since his term ended on May 15. Speaking while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening, Powell stated the Fed is undergoing a "stress test" with its credibility on the line.

Though Powell did not explicitly name the Trump administration in his remarks, the context made his concerns clear. The administration has taken several steps that challenge Fed independence, including launching a criminal investigation into the central bank's over-budget building renovation and attempting to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook.

Powell framed threats to Fed independence as dangers to an institution essential to American economic strength. The Federal Reserve has historically operated independently from political pressure to maintain public confidence in monetary policy decisions. This independence is considered fundamental to economic stability, allowing policymakers to base decisions on economic data rather than political considerations.

The timing of Powell's statement underscores his alarm about potential long-term damage to the Fed's reputation and effectiveness. Central banks worldwide depend on credibility to manage inflation expectations and preserve financial stability. Loss of public confidence in the Fed's independence could severely compromise its ability to fulfill its core mission.

Powell's decision to speak publicly immediately after leaving office is particularly significant. Though Fed leaders typically depart quietly after their terms conclude, Powell has announced he will remain on the Fed's board as a voting governor until the White House ends its scrutiny of the building renovation project. Powell characterized this scrutiny as "pretext" designed to pressure the central bank into lowering interest rates.

The former chair's warning comes as the Fed faces a transitional moment. Kevin Warsh, confirmed by the Senate on Wednesday in a 54-45 party-line vote, will take over as Fed chair on May 14. The confirmation was the most divisive in the position's history, with only one Democrat, Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, voting yes.

Warsh, a former Fed governor and Wall Street banker, has previously supported lower interest rates, echoing Trump's position. However, he will need to convince other members of the Fed's 12-member voting board to approve rate cuts. With inflation currently at 3.8%, making the case for lower rates could prove difficult.

At his Senate confirmation hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and remove politics from monetary policy. Yet his reluctance to answer whether Trump lost the 2020 election raised concerns among Democrats that he may prioritize political considerations over economic data.

Powell's warning reflects anxiety that the incoming administration may fundamentally alter how the central bank operates and makes decisions about interest rates and monetary policy.

cards.headline: Colombia presidential election heads to runoff between left and right candidates
cards.teaser: Left-wing senator Iván Cepeda will face pro-Trump candidate Abelardo de la Espriella in a runoff election.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election will proceed to a runoff after no candidate won a majority in the first round. Far-right lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella secured 43.7% of the vote, narrowly edging left-wing senator Iván Cepeda, who received 40.9%. The runoff is scheduled for June 21.

Cepeda, a philosopher and human rights activist, is backed by outgoing President Gustavo Petro. De la Espriella, a Trump admirer, has risen rapidly in the polls. The election comes a decade after Colombia signed a historic peace agreement with the FARC guerrilla group, with voters choosing between candidates offering starkly different visions for the country's future.

cards.headline: Two American media personalities banned from entering United Kingdom
cards.teaser: Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur were barred from entering the UK, with pro-Israel groups reportedly involved in the decision.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom banned American media personalities Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur from entering the country. Piker, a live-streamer, and Uygur, founder of The Young Turks, were both denied entry. Members of Parliament had urged the Home Office to revoke Piker's visa ahead of a scheduled speech in London, describing him as an extremist influencer who defended events of October 7.

Piker responded to the ban by criticizing what he called the significant power of pro-Israel groups in influencing the decision. The Home Office did not provide detailed public comments on the specific reasons for the entry bans. Both individuals have large online followings and produce left-wing political commentary for digital audiences.

cards.headline: China promotes surveillance technology and state control ideology abroad
cards.teaser: After perfecting a domestic surveillance state, China is exporting both the technology and ideology of state control to other nations.
cards.body:
China has spent decades developing and refining a comprehensive surveillance system within its own borders. Now the country is exporting both its surveillance technology and the ideology behind it to other nations around the world.

This expansion represents a significant shift in how China's domestic security apparatus is being leveraged internationally, allowing the country to promote its model of state control beyond its own population.

hero.headline: Man charged with murder in deaths of three men on Hawaii's Big Island
hero.body:
Jacob Baker has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with the deaths of three men on Hawaii's Big Island, according to the Hawaii Police Department. Baker faces nearly a dozen charges related to the killings.

The victims were three elderly men found dead on the Big Island. The Hawaii Police Department announced the charges against Baker in an official update, marking a significant development in the investigation.

Baker's arrest and charging represent the conclusion of the initial investigative phase into the deaths. The Hawaii Police Department has been working to piece together the circumstances surrounding the killings, which have shaken the Big Island community.

The charges against Baker include multiple offenses beyond the three murder counts, though the murder charges represent the most serious accusations he faces. Prosecutors will now move forward with the case against Baker as the legal process continues.

The case has drawn attention both locally in Hawaii and nationally as authorities work to bring justice for the three victims. The Big Island community has been waiting for answers since the deaths were first reported, and the formal charges mark a step forward in the criminal justice process.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that President Trump's name must come off the Kennedy Center, prompting a response from the president.
cards.body:
A federal judge issued an order requiring the removal of President Trump's name from the Kennedy Center. The decision blocks changes Trump had made to the Washington performing arts venue.

President Trump responded to the ruling, expressing frustration about the judge's decision. The legal battle over the Kennedy Center's name continues as the administration considers its next steps in the dispute.

cards.headline: Senate candidate Graham Platner addresses reports of sexually explicit messages
cards.teaser: Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner responded to news reports about sexually explicit texts he sent to multiple women while married.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, a Democratic candidate for the Maine US Senate seat, is facing scrutiny after reports that he sent sexually explicit text messages to multiple women while married. His wife alerted his campaign to the messages.

The revelations have prompted concern among prominent Democrats. Senator Cory Booker said he has "concerns" about Platner's campaign, stating that "that guy has questions to answer – and that's what campaigns are for." The situation has raised worries within the party about the race's viability.

cards.headline: White House releases results of Trump's physical exam
cards.teaser: President Trump's doctor released results from his latest physical examination, recommending weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
The White House released the results of President Trump's most recent physical examination. His doctor stated that Trump is in excellent health but recommended he lose weight and increase his exercise routine.

The medical report noted leg swelling and hand bruising.

cards.headline: Daily pill doubles survival time for pancreatic cancer patients
cards.teaser: A new drug called daraxonrasib has shown significant results in treating pancreatic cancer, the deadliest major cancer.
cards.body:
A daily pill called daraxonrasib has doubled survival time for pancreatic cancer patients in clinical trials, marking what experts describe as a "gamechanger" and one of the biggest breakthroughs in decades.

Pancreatic cancer remains the deadliest of all major cancers, with limited treatment options currently available. Most existing treatments provide little benefit to patients. The disease is often diagnosed late, after it has already spread to other parts of the body, affecting more than half of those diagnosed.

cards.headline: Remains found in New Mexico forest identified as missing woman
cards.teaser: New Mexico State Police identified remains found in Carson National Forest as those of Melissa Casias, who disappeared last year.
cards.body:
Remains discovered in Carson National Forest have been identified as Melissa Casias, a Taos woman who disappeared last year. New Mexico State Police confirmed the identification.

Casias worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory before her disappearance. The discovery brings closure to the search that began when she went missing.

cards.headline: Georgia towns challenge ICE detention center plans
cards.teaser: Small towns in Georgia are using a novel legal strategy to fight plans for an ICE detention facility, impressing legal experts.
cards.body:
Communities in Georgia are challenging a planned immigration detention center using a novel legal strategy. The town of Social Circle filed a federal lawsuit against Trump administration plans to convert a warehouse into one of the largest immigration detention facilities in the US.

Their complaint invokes public nuisance law, an approach that goes further than other recent lawsuits opposing detention centers. Those cases typically rely on arguments about missing environmental impact assessments required under the National Environmental Policy Act. Legal scholars say Social Circle's strategy could significantly influence how other communities challenge federal immigration detention proposals.

cards.headline: UAW Declares Strike at American Axle Plant Supplying General Motors
cards.teaser: The United Auto Workers union called a strike at an American Axle plant that supplies parts for General Motors trucks.
cards.body:
The UAW announced a strike at American Axle beginning at midnight, according to the Detroit Free Press and the union itself. The plant is described as a key supplier to General Motors, particularly for truck production. The Wall Street Journal identified the facility as critical to GM's supply chain.

WOODTV.com reported that a strike threat had been looming as a contract deadline approached. Wilcox Newspapers confirmed that UAW workers at the American Axle facility in Three Rivers went on strike. The action could disrupt production of GM trucks if the plant produces components with limited inventory buffers.

cards.headline: Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell Warns Fed Credibility at Risk
cards.teaser: Jerome Powell said the Federal Reserve's credibility would be lost if a president could fire its officials.
cards.body:
Powell delivered remarks warning that the Fed's credibility is at risk, according to Axios. Bloomberg reported that Powell said the central bank's credibility would be lost if the president gained the power to fire Federal Reserve officials. The Wall Street Journal described the warning as pointed but wrapped in abstraction.

The Boston Globe and Star Tribune reported that Powell accepted a JFK Profile in Courage award alongside Minnesota Twin Cities community leaders. Powell previously served as Federal Reserve chair before stepping down. His comments come as the Fed's independence has faced scrutiny from political figures seeking more influence over monetary policy decisions.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Earns $82 Million in Opening Weekend
cards.teaser: The horror movie Backrooms, made by a 20-year-old filmmaker for $10 million, sold $82 million in tickets.
cards.body:
Young Moviegoers Power 'Backrooms' to $82 Million in Ticket Sales. The horror film, which cost $10 million and came from a 20-year-old filmmaker, added to evidence that young people will go to theaters for the right offering.

The film's $82 million opening weekend demonstrates the commercial viability of low-budget horror productions when they resonate with younger audiences. Horror continues to draw theatrical crowds, particularly among viewers who value the communal cinema experience that scary films provide.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Flat as June Trading Begins Near Record Highs
cards.teaser: Stock futures traded flat in overnight sessions as June began with markets near record levels.
cards.body:
Stock futures showed little movement in overnight trading as June opened near record highs. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures all climbed after May ended with record closes.

Markets maintained elevated levels heading into the new month, with stocks closing out May on a strong note.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Move Higher Amid Uncertainty Over Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil climbed as signs remained elusive that a deal with Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran talks. The extended ceasefire agreement, which remains subject to Donald Trump's approval, prompted the decline in global oil prices.

Earlier market movements had seen oil climb due to concerns about the Strait of Hormuz and supply disruptions tied to the Iran situation. The shifting prices reflect traders reassessing supply risks as diplomatic developments emerged.

hero.headline: Dell launches $699 XPS 13 laptop to compete with Apple's MacBook Neo
hero.body:
Dell has announced a new XPS 13 laptop designed to challenge Apple's entry-level MacBook Neo. The device will launch in July with an introductory student price of $599, though this promotional pricing runs only until September. After the back-to-school period ends, the laptop will cost $699 for general consumers.

The MacBook Neo, Apple's newest entry-level offering, starts at $599 and represents a significant shift in Apple's laptop strategy. It uses the A18 Pro chip from the iPhone 16 Pro rather than Apple's traditional M-series processors. The MacBook Neo features a 13-inch LCD screen with a resolution of 2408x1506 pixels, 8GB of RAM, and either 256GB or 512GB of storage. It weighs 1.23kg and measures 12.7mm thick.

Apple's MacBook Neo delivers strong performance for everyday tasks despite its lower specifications compared to other Mac models. The device manages approximately 13 hours of battery life during general use including browsing, note-taking, image editing, and email. The keyboard and trackpad maintain the quality standards of higher-end MacBooks, though the base model lacks Touch ID, which only comes with the more expensive 512GB storage option.

The MacBook Neo includes features that some budget laptops omit, such as a headphone jack, mechanical trackpad, and 1080p webcam. However, it has some limitations. The screen lacks True Tone technology and the port selection is restricted, with only one USB-C port supporting USB3 speeds. Neither USB-C port supports Thunderbolt, and the device cannot drive displays higher than 4K at 60Hz.

Dell's new XPS 13 positions itself as an alternative for budget-conscious laptop buyers. The company has traditionally positioned the XPS line as a premium product, but this model represents a significant price reduction aimed at capturing customers who might otherwise choose Apple's entry-level option.

Both laptops target similar buyers: those seeking a lightweight, well-built machine for everyday computing without the premium price tag of higher-end models. The MacBook Neo comes preloaded with macOS 26 Tahoe and includes Apple's suite of free applications such as Pages, Numbers, Keynote, and iMovie, giving users productivity and creative software from the start.

The competition between these two devices reflects broader changes in the laptop market, where manufacturers are increasingly focused on delivering capable machines at accessible price points. Dell's timing with the XPS 13 announcement suggests the company sees genuine market demand at this price level, particularly among students and young professionals evaluating their options during back-to-school season.

cards.headline: AMD extends Socket AM5 platform support through 2029
cards.teaser: AMD committed to supporting its Socket AM5 platform until 2029, offering extended compatibility for future processors.
cards.body:
AMD announced that its Socket AM5 platform will receive support through 2029, giving customers a longer upgrade path for their motherboards. The company also revealed two new processors: the Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition and the Ryzen 7 7700X3D. The Anniversary Edition celebrates a decade of the AM4 platform.

The extended support timeline means users who purchase AM5 motherboards can expect compatibility with new AMD processors for several more years. AMD's strategy emphasizes platform longevity, allowing customers to upgrade their CPUs without replacing motherboards. The company is simultaneously reviving older Ryzen 7 5800X3D processors as part of its platform anniversary celebration.

cards.headline: Alienware unveils 39-inch 5K OLED monitor with RGB stripe panel
cards.teaser: Alienware released the AW3926QW, the first 39-inch 5K OLED monitor to use an RGB stripe panel.
cards.body:
Alienware announced the AW3926QW at Computex 2026, marking the world's first 39-inch 5K OLED monitor featuring an RGB stripe panel. The display succeeds Alienware's original QD-OLED gaming monitor from 2022, offering a refreshed design with upgraded specifications.

The 39-inch ultrawide format combines the resolution and color technology with the RGB stripe subpixel arrangement, which differs from traditional OLED configurations. Alienware is releasing multiple new OLED monitors as part of its 30th anniversary celebration, with the AW3926QW and other models arriving at different points throughout the year.

cards.headline: Nvidia N1x chip trails Apple M3 Max in early benchmark tests
cards.teaser: Pre-release Geekbench 6 scores show Nvidia's upcoming N1x processor performing below Apple's M3 Max chip from 2023.
cards.body:
Early benchmark results for Nvidia's N1x system-on-chip showed the processor underperforming compared to Apple's M3 Max chip, which launched in 2023. The first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips are scheduled to debut next week. Nvidia is holding a keynote at Computex where it may provide additional details about the N1x and N1 laptop processors.

The N1x and N1 chips represent Nvidia's entry into the laptop processor market, competing directly with Apple's custom silicon and established x86 processors from Intel and AMD. Specifications for both chips have begun circulating among technology publications. Some analysts suggest the Nvidia chips could provide new options for Windows devices, particularly Microsoft's Surface line.

cards.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 announced with October 23 launch date
cards.teaser: Activision revealed Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, promising a more authentic and grounded shooter experience.
cards.body:
Activision and Infinity Ward have announced Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, launching October 23 with campaign, multiplayer, and DMZ modes. The game imagines a present-day conflict involving Korea and marks a return to the grounded, controversial storytelling the franchise was historically known for.

The developer emphasized military authenticity as a core design principle. This shift away from recent entries' melodramatic approach positions Modern Warfare 4 in similar territory to earlier controversial entries like Modern Warfare 2's "No Russian" mission. Activision invited players to evaluate whether the game delivers on its promises of authentic gameplay.

cards.headline: Artist KC Green reaches agreement with AI startup over 'This is fine' meme use
cards.teaser: KC Green, creator of the 'This is fine' meme, reached an agreement with AI startup Artisan after the company used his artwork.
cards.body:
KC Green, the artist behind the widely recognized 'This is fine' meme, secured an agreement with AI startup Artisan. The startup used Green's meme in advertising materials and has since removed those ads. The resolution came after public attention to the unauthorized use of Green's copyrighted artwork.

The 'This is fine' meme, depicting a cartoon dog sitting in a burning room, has become one of the internet's most recognizable images. Green has worked to protect his intellectual property rights as companies increasingly use his artwork without permission. The agreement with Artisan represents another instance of creators enforcing their rights in an era where AI companies frequently use copyrighted material.

hero.headline: Knicks and Spurs to meet in NBA Finals, first matchup since 1999
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night, earning a trip to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks. The matchup marks the first time these two franchises will meet for the championship since 1999, when the Spurs won the series 4-1.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory with 22 points and seven rebounds in the decisive game. The 7-foot-4 French star was named the Western Conference Finals MVP and became emotional after clinching the Finals berth. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said when asked about his tears. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

Wembanyama's supporting cast also delivered crucial performances. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points and made six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper provided a spark off the bench. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup, made a key defensive play with a block in the fourth quarter as the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt.

The Thunder, defending NBA champions, struggled without guard Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, led Oklahoma City with 35 points and nine assists, but no other Thunder player scored more than 20 points. As the game neared its end, the Thunder were forced to take desperate three-pointers from well beyond the arc. The Spurs sealed the win with a breakaway dunk.

"You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said after the loss. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. But there's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

Julian Champagnie reflected on the Spurs' accomplishment after the game, saying "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen."

Game 1 of the NBA Finals between the Spurs and Knicks is set for Wednesday in San Antonio. The Spurs enter the series with historical advantage, having defeated the Knicks in their previous Finals meeting more than 25 years ago. The 1999 matchup remains the most recent Finals appearance for the Knicks, who have not won a championship since 1973.

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk upsets four-time champion Iga Swiatek at French Open
cards.teaser: Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk defeated defending champion Iga Swiatek at the French Open, guaranteeing a first-time women's champion.
cards.body:
Marta Kostyuk defeated four-time French Open champion Iga Swiatek in the round of 16, eliminating the last remaining former champion from the women's draw. The upset victory was part of a strong showing by Ukrainian players at the tournament.

With Swiatek's exit, the French Open will crown a new women's singles champion for the first time in years. The men's draw has also been cleared of previous champions, guaranteeing fresh titleholders in both singles categories.

cards.headline: Finland wins ice hockey world championship on Konsta Helenius overtime goal
cards.teaser: Konsta Helenius scored in overtime to give Finland the IIHF World Championship title.
cards.body:
Finland captured the IIHF World Championship after Konsta Helenius scored the golden goal in overtime. The 19-year-old forward's decisive strike secured the world title for Finland in dramatic fashion. Helenius, a prospect for the Buffalo Sabres, delivered the championship-winning moment in sudden-death overtime.

Florida Panthers forwards Aleksander Barkov and Anton Lundell were among the Finnish players who earned gold medals at the tournament. The victory gave Finland another world championship title, cementing their status as one of international hockey's elite programs. The overtime winner capped a tournament that saw Finland advance through each stage to claim the gold medal.

cards.headline: Joao Fonseca reaches French Open quarterfinals with win over Casper Ruud
cards.teaser: Rising star Joao Fonseca, 19, defeated two-time finalist Casper Ruud to advance to the French Open quarterfinals.
cards.body:
Joao Fonseca advanced to the French Open quarterfinals with a victory over two-time finalist Casper Ruud. The 19-year-old Brazilian's win came on the back of his earlier triumph over Novak Djokovic, demonstrating his credentials as a title contender at Roland Garros.

With previous French Open champions eliminated from the draw, a first-time men's champion will be crowned this year. Fonseca's back-to-back wins over top opponents have established him as one of the tournament's rising forces.

cards.headline: North Carolina advances to Super Regional after defeating East Carolina
cards.teaser: The Tar Heels beat East Carolina 9-3 to win the Chapel Hill Regional and advance to their 13th Super Regional.
cards.body:
North Carolina defeated East Carolina 9-3 in the regional final to advance to the NCAA baseball Super Regionals. The Tar Heels went 2-0 against ECU in the Chapel Hill Regional, clinching their 13th Super Regional appearance in program history. The victory eliminated the Pirates from the tournament.

North Carolina outlasted East Carolina in a decisive performance that secured their spot in the next round of the NCAA tournament. The Tar Heels will now prepare for Super Regional competition as they pursue a College World Series berth. East Carolina had been fighting to stave off elimination but could not overcome North Carolina's offensive output in the regional final.

cards.headline: Top-seeded UCLA eliminated from NCAA baseball tournament by Saint Mary's
cards.teaser: The number one national seed UCLA lost to Saint Mary's 3-2, ending the Bruins' season in a regional opener.
cards.body:
UCLA, the top overall seed in the NCAA baseball tournament, was eliminated after losing to Saint Mary's 3-2 in the opening game of their regional. The defeat at home ended the Bruins' national title hopes and marked one of four losses by national seeds on the opening day of regional play. Saint Mary's upset was among the tournament's biggest surprises.

The loss concluded UCLA's season after entering as the tournament's highest-ranked team. The Bruins were unable to capitalize on hosting the regional, falling to a Saint Mary's team that executed in a tight game. The opening day of regionals also featured two 14-inning marathon

hero.headline: R&B Singer Peabo Bryson Suffers Stroke
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning R&B singer known for his duets on Disney film soundtracks, has suffered a stroke and is receiving medical treatment, according to a statement from his representative.

Bryson, a two-time Grammy Award winner, provided the singing voice for two of Disney's most popular songs. He performed "A Whole New World" from Aladdin and the title track from Beauty and the Beast, both of which won Academy Awards. His representative confirmed the stroke to Variety but did not provide additional details about his condition or prognosis.

The veteran singer built a career as a balladeer and songwriter spanning several decades. His Disney collaborations brought his voice to a global audience and remain among the most recognized songs in the studio's catalog. Both tracks achieved significant commercial success and continue to be performed and recorded by artists worldwide.

Bryson's career extended beyond his Disney work. He recorded numerous albums as a solo artist and collaborated with other performers in the R&B genre. His vocal style and approach to romantic ballads established him as a distinctive voice in contemporary music.

The singer's representative did not specify when the stroke occurred or where Bryson is currently receiving treatment. No timeline has been provided for his recovery or future performances.

cards.headline: Euphoria Season 3 Finale Streams on HBO Max
cards.teaser: The HBO series concluded its third season with the finale episode now available for streaming.
cards.body:
The Season 3 finale of Euphoria, titled "In God We Trust," is now streaming on HBO Max. The episode brings closure to major character arcs, including Zendaya's Rue Bennett, with significant plot developments that reshape the season's storylines.

The finale features performances from Colman Domingo and Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje as Alamo Brown, whose character plays a pivotal role in the episode's climactic events. Creator Sam Levinson has provided commentary on the finale's major moments and character resolutions.

cards.headline: YouTuber Horror Film Backrooms Opens With $82 Million
cards.teaser: A horror film created by YouTube filmmakers earned more than $80 million in its opening weekend at the box office.
cards.body:
Backrooms, a horror film made by creators known for their YouTube work, debuted with ticket sales between $81 million and $82 million, according to box office reports. The strong performance was driven primarily by younger moviegoers.

The film's success comes as other recent releases showed mixed results. Another horror title, Obsession, experienced an unusual increase in its second weekend, while the Star Wars film The Mandalorian and Grogu saw a 70 percent drop from its opening. Industry observers have noted the emergence of a trend they describe as a zoomer-horror renaissance, with films from digital creators attracting significant theatrical audiences.

cards.headline: Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown Dead at 42
cards.teaser: Matt Brown, who appeared on the reality series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42, his family confirmed.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, a cast member of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, was found dead. His brother Bear Brown helped recover his body from a river, according to family statements reported by multiple outlets.

Brown had been spotted near a river where police said a man went missing. His family confirmed his death, though the exact circumstances were not fully detailed in initial reports. Brown was 42 or 43 years old, with sources providing slightly different ages.

cards.headline: M.I.A. Sues Kid Cudi for $2.8 Million Over Tour Dismissal
cards.teaser: The British rapper filed a lawsuit after being removed from Kid Cudi's concert tour.
cards.body:
M.I.A. has filed a lawsuit seeking $2.8 million from Kid Cudi after she was removed from his Rebel Ragers Tour. The rapper was dismissed from her opening act role after making remarks that Kid Cudi characterized as offensive.

A statement from M.I.A.'s team said Kid Cudi's actions represented attempts to silence freedom of artistic expression and speech. The lawsuit claims a breach of M.I.A.'s contract with Live Nation, which she says guaranteed her full creative control over her performance. Kid Cudi had previously stated he removed M.I.A. from the tour due to the nature of her remarks during performances.

cards.headline: John Oliver Criticizes Trump Freedom 250 Concert on Last Week Tonight
cards.teaser: The HBO host devoted a segment of his show to the Trump administration's 250th birthday concert series.
cards.body:
John Oliver used the opening of Last Week Tonight to criticize President Trump's Freedom 250 concert series, which celebrates America's 250th birthday. The event drew scrutiny from multiple HBO hosts, including Bill Maher, over its performer lineup and purpose.

Several musicians withdrew from the concert, citing concerns that the event would be political in nature. The departures prompted Trump to attack the artists who dropped out and consider appearing at the event himself, or potentially hosting a MAGA rally instead.

cards.headline: DirecTV Drops 54 Scripps Local Stations in 36 Markets
cards.teaser: A dispute between the satellite service and the broadcaster resulted in dozens of local television stations going dark.
cards.body:
DirecTV and Scripps Networks entered a retransmission dispute that resulted in 54 local Scripps television stations becoming unavailable to DirecTV subscribers across 36 markets. The blackout took effect at 7 p.m. Eastern Time.

Both companies blamed each other for the service interruption. DirecTV noted the timing of the blackout comes ahead of several state and local primary elections scheduled for June, as well as upcoming NBA playoff games. The affected stations represent a significant portion of Scripps' local broadcast network across Nielsen-designated television markets.

hero.headline: Powell warns Federal Reserve credibility at risk in first remarks since leaving office
hero.body:
Former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell has issued a stark warning that the central bank faces a credibility crisis in his first public comments since his term ended on May 15. Speaking while accepting the John F. Kennedy Profiles in Courage award on Sunday evening, Powell stated the Fed is undergoing a "stress test" with its credibility on the line.

Though Powell did not explicitly name the Trump administration in his remarks, the context made his concerns clear. The administration has taken several steps that challenge Fed independence, including launching a criminal investigation into the central bank's over-budget building renovation and attempting to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook.

Powell framed threats to Fed independence as dangers to an institution essential to American economic strength. The Federal Reserve has historically operated independently from political pressure to maintain public confidence in monetary policy decisions. This independence is considered fundamental to economic stability, allowing policymakers to base decisions on economic data rather than political considerations.

The timing of Powell's statement underscores his alarm about potential long-term damage to the Fed's reputation and effectiveness. Central banks worldwide depend on credibility to manage inflation expectations and preserve financial stability. Loss of public confidence in the Fed's independence could severely compromise its ability to fulfill its core mission.

Powell's decision to speak publicly immediately after leaving office is particularly significant. Though Fed leaders typically depart quietly after their terms conclude, Powell has announced he will remain on the Fed's board as a voting governor until the White House ends its scrutiny of the building renovation project. Powell characterized this scrutiny as "pretext" designed to pressure the central bank into lowering interest rates.

The former chair's warning comes as the Fed faces a transitional moment. Kevin Warsh, confirmed by the Senate on Wednesday in a 54-45 party-line vote, will take over as Fed chair on May 14. The confirmation was the most divisive in the position's history, with only one Democrat, Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, voting yes.

Warsh, a former Fed governor and Wall Street banker, has previously supported lower interest rates, echoing Trump's position. However, he will need to convince other members of the Fed's 12-member voting board to approve rate cuts. With inflation currently at 3.8%, making the case for lower rates could prove difficult.

At his Senate confirmation hearing, Warsh pledged to maintain Fed independence and remove politics from monetary policy. Yet his reluctance to answer whether Trump lost the 2020 election raised concerns among Democrats that he may prioritize political considerations over economic data.

Powell's warning reflects anxiety that the incoming administration may fundamentally alter how the central bank operates and makes decisions about interest rates and monetary policy.

cards.headline: Pence criticizes Trump for abandoning conservative principles
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence challenged President Trump's conservative credentials in a Wall Street Journal op-ed.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence criticized President Trump for shifting away from conservative principles toward populist policies. In an op-ed published in the Wall Street Journal, Pence described a transformation in Trump's tone and rhetoric that now emphasizes widespread reform through populist measures.

Pence expressed concerns about what he characterized as Trump's abandonment of his conservative base. He also referenced Trump's attempt to pressure him during the certification of the 2020 election results, suggesting broader concerns about constitutional order. The public criticism from Pence represents a significant break with the president he once served.

cards.headline: Paxton to meet Senate leadership after primary upset of Cornyn
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton will meet with Senate Majority Leader John Thune after defeating incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a GOP runoff.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said he will meet with Senate Majority Leader John Thune following his victory over four-term incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican runoff. Paxton's win represents a major upset in Texas Republican politics, unseating a long-serving senator.

Paxton said he has been in contact with Thune, Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, and Republican Conference Chair Tom Cotton since winning the runoff. The meeting with Senate leadership will mark Paxton's transition from state attorney general to preparing for a role in the U.S. Senate.

cards.headline: More than 10,000 federal lawyers have left government since 2024
cards.teaser: President Trump said it is good that thousands of lawyers have departed federal service, responding to a New York Times report on the exodus.
cards.body:
More than 10,000 lawyers working for the federal government have left their positions between the end of 2024 and March, according to reporting by the New York Times. The departures represent a significant loss of legal talent across federal agencies.

President Trump responded to the Times report by saying it is very good that thousands of lawyers have chosen to leave the administration. His comment suggests he views the departure of legal staff as beneficial rather than concerning. The exodus affects multiple agencies and departments across the federal government.

cards.headline: Family visits resume at New Jersey detention center after protests
cards.teaser: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill announced that the Department of Homeland Security will restore family visitation at a Newark detention facility.
cards.body:
Family visitation at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark is being restored after a week of heated protests, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and federal homeland security officials announced Sunday. The visitation cancellation had followed a hunger strike by detainees at the facility.

However, families of detained immigrants faced confusion about which detainees would be eligible for visits following the announcement. Local officials also imposed an indefinite overnight curfew starting at 9pm in a blocked-off area surrounding Delaney Hall.

cards.headline: Democratic Party chair faces pressure over 2024 election review
cards.teaser: DNC Chair Ken Martin confronts growing criticism over the party's handling of its 2024 election analysis and financial challenges.
cards.body:
Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin is facing mounting pressure from party members over the committee's handling of its 2024 election review and ongoing financial difficulties. Critics within the party have questioned Martin's leadership as Democrats begin planning for the 2028 presidential race.

The controversy centers on what some Democrats describe as a bungled autopsy of the 2024 election and the DNC's financial struggles. Martin has so far avoided a formal revolt among DNC members, even as they work to establish the calendar for the 2028 presidential primary. The leadership dispute represents the earliest major test of party unity heading into the next election cycle.

cards.headline: Pence says efforts underway to rewrite January 6 history
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence said there has been a clear effort to revise the historical record of the Capitol riot.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said there has "clearly" been an effort to "rewrite" the history of the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot. He expressed confidence that history will ultimately judge the events accurately.

Pence's comments come as he has also criticized President Trump in recent statements, questioning his conservative credentials and what Pence describes as Trump's "hostility to constitutional order." As vice president, Pence presided over the joint session of Congress certifying the 2020 election and refused to interfere with the electoral count despite becoming a target of rioters.
